attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: Discover

steps.text: Watch this video to learn about using the Assets menu to create and store custom tiles, images, tilemaps, and animations to build tilemap projects in JavaScript!

questions.hint: What else can you create using the Assets menu?
questions.title: What types of assets can be created using the Assets menu?
questions.correctResponse: You can create and save images, animations, tiles, tilemaps, and songs using the Assets menu!

questions.hint: What symbols and syntax are needed to correctly use an asset?
questions.title: [Select one] Which chunk of code uses the correct syntax to access an image asset?
questions.correctResponse: In order to use an asset in a project, type asset, a dot operator, the asset type, and the asset name surrounded by backticks ``.

questions.hint: Which line of code uses the correct syntax to access a tile asset?
questions.title: [Select one] Which line of code correctly places the sprite on a tile asset?
questions.correctResponse: In order to use an asset in a project, type asset, a dot operator, the asset type, and the asset name surrounded by backticks ``.

questions.hint: What symbols and syntax are needed to correctly use an asset in a project?
questions.title: [Match one per answer] Match the part of the code to its name: assets.image`playerSprite`
questions.correctResponse: In order to use an asset in a project, type asset, a dot operator, the asset type, and the asset name surrounded by backticks ``.

questions.title: [Open response] What is something you’re looking forward to creating with assets and tilemaps?
questions.correctResponse: Those sound like great ideas! Looking forward to seeing what you create with assets and tilemaps in Brown Belt!

subgroups.title: Asset Management!
subgroups.introduction: Watch this video to learn about using the Assets menu to create and store custom tiles, images, tilemaps, and animations to build tilemap projects in JavaScript!

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about using the Assets menu to create and manage assets in a project, including tilemaps. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: Asset Management
badges.description: Use the Assets menu in the code editor, and use tilemap code and assets in a project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Carefully Curated
badges.description: Use the Assets menu to organize image, tile, and tilemap assets.

badges.title: Art Re-Collecting
badges.description: Access image, tile, and tilemap assets from My Assets in the code editor.

badges.title: Drop a Pin
badges.description: Position sprites on a tilemap using JavaScript.

badges.title: Lights, Camera, Action!
badges.description: Write code to use the camera functions in JavaScript.
